approved: Proposed consequential amendments to establish the DisabilityCare Australia Fund, supporting the government's increase of the Medicare levy from 1.5 to two per cent of taxable income, and enabling the Future Fund to manage the fund and reimburse states through the COAG Reform Fund.

Supported the DisabilityCare Australia Fund (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013, which manages Medicare levy revenue raised by an increase from 1.4 to two per cent expected to reach $11.4 billion over the forward estimates and an estimated $20.4 billion by 2018-19, and said the coalition would establish a joint parliamentary committee to oversee the National Disability Insurance Scheme's implementation if elected.

Supported the DisabilityCare Australia Fund bill, saying 11,000 Tasmanians will receive support under the scheme, and drew parallels with Medicare, noting the Fraser government gutted Medibank in October 1976 before Labor reintroduced universal healthcare in 1984, and quoted the member for Warringah's 1995 description of compulsory superannuation as a con job to warn against a change of government.

Moved to close debate on the DisabilityCare Australia Fund (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013, saying support was necessary to provide certainty to the disability sector through transparent and accountable funding of the NDIS, and commended the bill to the House.
